slides.headline: October 27, 1904: a revolutionary was born who would die 63 days into a hunger strike, demanding dignity for political prisoners.
Jatindra Nath Das was born in Calcutta on October 27, 1904
slides.body: Arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case alongside Bhagat Singh, he launched a hunger strike in Lahore Jail on July 13, 1929, demanding Indian political prisoners get the same treatment as European prisoners - better food, reading material, and no humiliating searches.

slides.headline: He died 63 days into the strike, on September 13, 1929, at age 24.
slides.body: His death triggered mass protests and funeral processions across India, and is credited with influencing how political detainees were treated in prisons for years afterward.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat remembers that dignity in its institutions was fought for, not handed down.
slides.body: Das never lived to see independence - but the standard he died demanding became part of how a free India would later treat anyone in its custody.

sources.text: Sabrang India - Remembering the independence activist, Jatindra Nath Das
